t49.content:
Dinner was everything the evening promised — warm food, candlelight, and Mira laughing at things she'd never admit were funny. For a few hours, the King of Curses, the rank evaluation, and the weight of a summoned hero's destiny simply... didn't exist. Just two people sharing a table.

You walk her back to the guild under a sky thick with stars, and when you take her hand and press your lips to her knuckles, she doesn't pull away. She just looks at you with that complicated expression — the one you're starting to think means *you're impossible and I don't entirely hate it.*

**Mira:** "Don't be late tomorrow, Soren."

You find Tempest curled in a side street like a small mountain, surrounded by flowers someone apparently left him, snoring with the deep satisfaction of a creature who found three lost cats, helped unload a merchant's cart, and carried two elderly women home from the market. You climb onto his warm scales, use his wing as a blanket, and close your eyes.

Sukuna says nothing. Even he recognizes when a night is simply *good.*

Sleep comes fast. Tomorrow, the rank evaluation board decides who you are in this world. Tonight, you already know.

t50.content: The morning rises. I awaken as the sun shines and I do some stretches and a quick workout before making sure my clothes are okay. I then turn to tempest who has just woken up as I say to him "Okay bud another big day! Get out there and make a difference!" I smile at him as I wave and he heads off to go find citizens to help. After a few minutes I have made my way into the guild where Mira,brom and the entire guild are ready to rank me. I stare at Mira and wink at her as the guild begins to evaluate me and will finish its evaluation of me completely.

t51.content:
Dawn breaks golden over the Capital City's rooftops, and you're already moving — stretches, shadowboxing, a few controlled bursts of cursed energy that make the cobblestones hum beneath your feet. Tempest blinks his enormous yellow eyes at you sleepily, then rumbles something that sounds suspiciously like *"already?"* before unfurling his wings and lumbering off to find citizens who need help. You smooth your black shirt, check your white pants — presentable enough for a hero — and head to the guild.

Inside, the entire hall has been rearranged. Tables pushed back, chairs in rows, the Guild Board seated at the front like a very serious panel of people trying to evaluate something that defies evaluation. Mira stands at the center, arms crossed, a thick folder of papers in her grip. She catches your wink and her mouth does that complicated thing again.

**[Mira:** "Right. Soren. The board has reviewed your contract completion — unconventional as it was — your combat display, witness testimonies, and..." she pauses, glancing at the papers, "...approximately fourteen separate incident reports from yesterday alone."]

The guild murmurs. Brom grins from the back row.

**[Mira:** "By unanimous decision — and I want it noted I voted *reluctantly* — you are hereby ranked **B-Class, Special Designation: Irregular.** Don't make me regret this."]

The hall erupts. Someone in the back throws their drink.

t52.content: I raise a finger as I say "Umm beautiful no one seen me take on tempest before I tamed him...I'm not ungrateful but I request politely for a re-evaluation. Allow me to show you all personal what I can do it combat so that I may have a higher rank!"

t53.content:
Mira stops mid-step. Her arm, still linked with yours, goes very still.

She turns to look at you with the expression of a woman calculating exactly how much paperwork this is going to generate.

**Mira:** "You tamed a wyvern solo, conjured gold from thin air, and walked into MY guild with Ryomen Sukuna living in your chest — and *now* you want a higher evaluation."

It isn't a question. It's a woman staring into the abyss.

A beat of silence. Then the Dwarf, who apparently followed them outside, calls from the guild doorway:

**Dwarf:** "I WANT TO SEE IT."

Mira closes her eyes. Opens them. Looks at you with something that might be exhaustion, might be respect, might be the early stages of a headache she'll blame on you specifically for the next decade.

**Mira:** "Fine. Tomorrow morning. The guild arena. You perform — *properly* — in front of the evaluation panel." She points a finger at your nose. "But tonight? Dinner first. Business second. Non-negotiable."

She takes your arm again and starts walking like the matter is entirely settled.

t54.content: "What? I'm confused? You and I had dinner last night Mira and the day just began...like I slept on tempest in the middle of the street because I told you I had no where to sleep.... The day just began and I come in for the evaluation that's what we discussed last night so I vote brom and some more if your more competent guild members try their hands at combat with me. Effective immediately if it's not to much to ask. So that I can show you I am so much more than you all have seen so far!"

t144.content: "Yes ma'am we are and along with myself,the leader of our group brom here,ryn,cael,and Daven we also have a merchant and his two kids. I respectfully ask you feed and house them and our adventure group for the night!"

t145.content:
The Guard Sergeant — a broad-shouldered woman with a sun-weathered face and the permanent squint of someone who's seen every border scam in the book — looks past you at the assembled group. Her eyes tick across each face: Brom's gap-toothed grin, Ryn's hand resting easy on her sword hilt, Cael's scholarly fidgeting, Daven's road-worn composure. Then the merchant, one arm still favoring his healed side, with Lena and Kai pressed close behind him.

She exhales through her nose. A long, deliberate exhale.

**[Guard Sergeant: "** "B-Class credentials check out. Merchant's transit papers?" **"]**

She holds out her hand without looking away from Soren — the universal gesture of *I don't entirely trust you but the paperwork says I should.*

The pass behind her is bustling with midday activity: a stone garrison building sits to the left, smoke curling from a cookfire, and the unmistakable smell of something hearty drifting through the gate archway. Housing exists. Food exists. Whether she grants it depends on this next moment.

She raises one eyebrow. Waiting.

t146.content: I look to brom as he steps up and hands her the correct papers given to us by Mira.

t147.content:
Brom steps up beside you with a practiced ease — the kind of man who's handed over paperwork at a dozen border crossings and learned to do it without making eye contact. He produces the merchant's transit documents from his vest pocket and holds them out toward the Guard Sergeant with a gap-toothed smile.

**[Brom: "** "Caravan out of the Capital. Merchant goods, six escorts, two civilian passengers. B-Class guild authorization signed by Guild Master Mira herself — you'll see the seal on the bottom left."**"]**

The Guard Sergeant takes the papers with a weathered hand and unfolds them slowly. Her eyes track across the text with the practiced efficiency of someone who has read ten thousand of these and caught three forgeries.

She pauses. Glances up at you. Then back at the papers.

**[Guard Sergeant: "** "B-Class Irregular."**"]** It isn't a question. She says it the way people say *'so the rumors were true.'*

The gates behind her are iron-banded oak, thick as a man's torso — and they are *very* closed. Beyond them lies the northeast territories, open road, and the return journey home.

She taps the papers against her palm once. Twice.

t148.content: "Look I just wanna make sure the merchant and his two kids my friends and I have picked up can eat and sleep somewhere safe so please for all that is holy stop eye fucking me and let us pass...Mira is all the woman I'll ever need.

t149.content:
The Guard Sergeant blinks. Once. Twice. His mustache twitches with the effort of a man recalibrating his entire afternoon.

**Guard Sergeant:** "I— yes. Fine. *Fine.*" He straightens his posture with wounded dignity and stamps the travel documents with more force than strictly necessary. "Merchant, two children, and..." he glances at Brom's group, "...whatever *this* collection of individuals is. Cleared for passage."

He slides the papers back without meeting your eyes.

**Guard Sergeant:** "...And tell no one I was— I was simply doing my *job*. Standard procedure. Nothing else."

Behind you, Brom muffles an enormous laugh into his fist. Cael is writing something in his notebook. Ryn is staring at the middle distance with the expression of someone who has accepted their life choices.

The Stone Gates groan open — heavy iron and old timber swinging wide to reveal the border settlement beyond: a cluster of warm buildings, lamplight already flickering in the late midday sun, and the unmistakable smell of bread and stew drifting from what is clearly a tavern.

Lena grabs her brother Kai's hand. The merchant exhales for what sounds like the first time in three days.

The caravan rolls through.

t150.content: I stare at brom as I say "That guard was a woman not a man...that's why I said what I said!"
